key_insight: R3MG-C is a high-order algebraic-geometric multilevel preconditioner that uses only finite-element support-point coordinates to build robust coarse spaces for continuous high-order discretizations.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical alternative to standard AMG when high-order FEM systems become difficult to precondition, helping keep solver iterations stable in real engineering simulations.
method: Recursively partitions support points with an R-tree using axis-aligned bounding boxes to form agglomerates.
Builds prolongation and Galerkin levels automatically from these agglomerates, without a prescribed mesh hierarchy.
Uses local discontinuous polynomial coarse spaces of degree p'>0, transferred through continuous nodal interpolation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports two- and three-dimensional numerical experiments where the V-cycle preconditioner maintains stable iteration counts even in regimes where standard AMG deteriorates.
watch_item: Performance depends on assumptions such as uniform box-regularity, interpolation stability, and stable decomposition, so robustness may vary on highly irregular geometries or partitions.
paper_title: R3MG-C: a high-order algebraic-geometric multilevel preconditioner for continuous finite element discretizations
